items.note: Page (published 09.09.2025) confirms: Gemeindeausschuss decided unanimously on 20 Dec 2022 to adjust the Blue Zone tariffs; Zone A 2.50 EUR/h, Zone B 1.50 EUR/h; 6-month subscription 180 EUR (first) and 270 EUR (second), 12-month 280 and 420 EUR; takes effect at the start of 2023. Two wordings are not on the page: it says first and second 'Abonnement' (subscription), not first and second car, and it does not say these are resident subscriptions (the ordinance elsewhere ties subscriptions to residents without a private space). The page describes an adjustment ('Anpassung'), it does not say prices were raised. The city's own 'Parkgebühren' link points to this same page, and the page does not say the rates are still in force in 2026.
items.corrected_text: The municipal executive (Gemeindeausschuss) unanimously decided on 20 December 2022 to adjust the Blue Park tariffs, taking effect at the start of 2023. The page lists 2.50 euro per hour in Zone A and 1.50 euro in Zone B, and subscriptions of 180 euro (6 months) and 280 euro (12 months) for the first subscription, 270 and 420 euro for the second. The page does not say whether these rates are still current in 2026.

items.note: Page (published 13.02.2023, last updated 13.05.2026) says Zone A is paid daily and Zone B Monday to Saturday, marked by signs and blue markings; subscriptions for residents without a private space, social institutions and people with disabilities; street list included in the document and an annex PDF is attached. I also opened the ordinance PDF itself (Italian/German): Art. 3 gives Zone A Monday-Sunday 08:00-19:00 and Zone B Monday-Saturday 08:00-19:00, and it also defines a Zone C reserved for tourist coaches paid 0:00-24:00; the ordinance was approved by resolution 103 of 21.12.2022 and amended by resolutions of 13.02.2023 and 28.04.2026. So the zone hours are settled: the ordinance resolves the conflict with item 2 (Zone A daily, Zone B Mon-Sat).

Page (published 25.12.2023, last updated 07.05.2026) says blue-marked spaces along streets and squares are paid Monday to Sunday 08:00-19:00 (not simply 'daily' for all blue spaces: the ordinance, page and PDF, says Zone B is paid only Monday to Saturday, so the page's blanket statement is too general). Tickets at nearby machines or via mobile payment apps; the line 'only the actual parking time is paid' appears in the mobile-app paragraph, not as a statement for machines. It says garage locations and space availability can be found at mobility.meran.eu, and links to the Stadtparkraumkonzept. Date 2026-05-07 matches the last update.
items.corrected_text: As of the page's last update on 7 May 2026, the city says blue-marked street spaces are paid Monday to Sunday from 08:00 to 19:00, with tickets bought at nearby machines or paid by mobile apps (a virtual ticket is issued for the licence plate and only the actual parking time is paid). The city's Blue Park ordinance, however, makes Zone B paid only Monday to Saturday, so the page's blanket statement is simplified. The page points to mobility.meran.eu for locations and free spaces of the large city-centre car parks and links an urban parking concept (Stadtparkraumkonzept).

items.note: Page (published 25.12.2023, last updated 06.05.2026) confirms several ZTLs in the city centre monitored by fully automated cameras at four positions (Postbrucke, Obere Freiheitsstrasse/Theaterplatz, Galileistrasse after the Algunder Kellerei car park, Zenobergstrasse/Passeirer Tor), digital-only checks, automatic fines, disability-card holders may apply. The authorised list includes all Merano taxis and the vehicles of 'Anrainer' (adjacent residents/frontagers), only within permitted times and following the signs; the draft says plain 'residents' and drops that qualifier.
items.corrected_text: The city centre has several restricted traffic zones (ZTL) monitored by fully automated cameras at four points: Postbrucke, Obere Freiheitsstrasse/Theaterplatz, Galileistrasse after the Algunder Kellerei car park, and Zenobergstrasse (Passeirer Tor). All Merano taxis and the vehicles of Anrainer (adjacent residents) are on the authorised list, only within permitted times and following the signs, and people with a disability card can apply for a permit. Checks are digital only and fines are issued automatically (page last updated 6 May 2026).

items.note: Italian city page (undated; item date is the approval date): PUMS approved by council resolution no. 11 of 11.03.2025, PGTU by council resolution no. 12 of 11.03.2025; documents are linked via Padlet. The page mentions regulation of stationary traffic only generically (PUMS topics) and describes no concrete parking measures, as the draft says.

City press release published and last updated 07.10.2026. Confirms: strategic concept 'Kurstadt 2.0'; first city-centre measures from January 2027 (traffic-calmed zones in Rennweg, lower Freiheitsstrasse and heavy traffic in Obermais, reversed flows in Alpini- and Huberstrasse and part of Manzonistrasse, reorganisation of parking in the central area in connection with the new Kavernengarage); opening ceremony of the bypass on 21 November, release to traffic on 26 November 2026; shuttle-bus link (mobility centre, hospital, Rennweg, thermal baths, Untermais station) is described as an idea presented. All worded as plans, as in the draft. Note the release gives no opening date or price for the Kavernengarage.

Same 07.10.2026 release: the presentation noted the existing hospital car park is fully used on weekdays in school time between about 07:30 and 12:00; under the Cura Resort project about 700 spaces are planned, 155 more than now (the draft's 'plan for the health area' is a loose but acceptable label).

Suedtirol News, 1 Feb 2024: PPP project, funds fully raised by private partners in return for a 50-year concession granted by the municipality; cost rose from 27 to 39 million euro; 594 spaces, 12 EV charging stations, several car-sharing spaces; garage accessible only once the second bypass lot (tunnel) is finished, 'not before 2026'. Article names the bidder group (Central Parking spa with others), not Meran Centrum Parking AG; that name is from item 9.

Alto Adige, 14 Feb 2019: definitive agreement between the Comune and the Central Parking-led group (council vote still due 20-21 March 2019); maximum hourly rate 2.40 euro adjustable for inflation; monthly pass not above 183 euro; payment to the city for up to 300 eliminated blue-park spaces at 150 euro per space per year for the first 15 years (then 300, then 600 euro). The draft's wording 'reported terms' and 'final contract terms were not checked' is appropriate.

Salto, 11 Feb 2025: Meran Centrum Parking AG is the investor group implementing the PPP Kavernengarage together with the municipality; tunnel opening to traffic planned for autumn 2026, with the Kavernengarage to open at the same time (statement by Strimmer, head of the provincial road office); the municipality has invested about 6 million euro on securing works as the concession contract provides, versus 3.7 million estimated about two years earlier.

Read the Landtag PDF (written question, signed 10.08.2026, protocol LTG_0005103 of 11.08.2026) with pypdf. It gives 347,598 vehicles parked 'im letzten Jahr' in the Therme Meran garage, parking as third-largest revenue item at more than 2.3 million euro after pools & sauna and gastronomy. The party is not stated in the document (signatories Madeleine Rohrer, Brigitte Foppa, Zeno Oberkofler), so 'Green' MPs is not on the page. The revenue statement is conditional: revenue 'dürften sinken' after tunnel and garage open, 'provided motorised traffic is actually banned from the inner city'. The question also says the tunnel is to open in November 2026. No reply is on the page.
items.corrected_text: In a written question to the provincial government (dated 10 August 2026), three South Tyrol Landtag members (Madeleine Rohrer, Brigitte Foppa and Zeno Oberkofler) state that 347,598 vehicles parked in the Therme Meran underground garage in the previous year and that parking brought in more than 2.3 million euro, the third-largest revenue item of the baths after pools and sauna and catering. They say revenue is likely to fall once the tunnel and Kavernengarage open, provided motorised traffic is really banned from the city centre. These are the MPs' figures; no reply was found.

items.note: Operator FAQ (undated; read October 2026): with a day ticket, visitors can pay an extra 16 euro to park until midnight; with 2-3 hour tickets the first hour is free and each further hour costs 3.20 euro; the 16 euro day option is not available during the entire Advent and Christmas season (the first hour stays included then). Undated page, so worded as 'on the operator's FAQ' is right; date 2026-10 is the retrieval month.

St. Josef page (undated, though the site's news list runs to 06.10.2026): 90 public, wide, video-monitored spaces, 2 EV charging stations, open 24 h, 1.40 euro per half hour (07:00-20:00) and 0.90 euro per half hour (20:00-07:00), billed in 30-minute steps, entry height 2.15 m. Date 2026-10 is the retrieval month. Operator's own advertising, medium confidence is fair.

Suedtirol News, 6 Sep 2023: on behalf of the city, Neogy (Alperia and Dolomiti Energia) set up 18 new charging columns at eleven locations; starting point six public columns with twelve charge points; target 50 public charge points by 2025; planned charging hub at Untermais station with 3 hyperchargers and 3 fast 22 kW columns (twelve charge points in total). The article adds that most of the tendered infrastructure was already built in 2023, with only the Untermais hub and one other site still missing, so 'commissioned to install' understates progress slightly but is not wrong.

Suedtirol News, 30 Dec 2024: the provincial government gave the go-ahead for planning and implementation of the mobility centre at the station site; about 350 parking spaces for commuters reachable underground; about 1,000 covered bike spaces; about 28.4 million euro (16.5 million from the national development and cohesion fund, over 11.9 million from the province). The article itself says planning in 2025 and realisation in 2026. The claim that the schedule 'has since slipped to 2028-2029' is not on this page; it comes from the city's 7 Oct 2026 release (item 5's page), which gives a construction period of about two years between 2028 and 2029 and mentions a new underground car park for commuters, so it is true but belongs to a different source. Whether the cost is still current in 2026 is not stated.
items.corrected_text: On 30 December 2024 the provincial government gave the start signal for planning and building a new mobility centre on the railway station site. The report describes about 350 parking spaces reachable underground, mainly for commuters, about 1,000 covered bike spaces, and a cost of about 28.4 million euro (16.5 million from the national development and cohesion fund, over 11.9 million from the province). The report said planning would start in 2025 and realisation in 2026.

items.note: City page last updated 02.10.2025: Stadtwerke Meran AG builds and operates infrastructure including water supply, environmental services, public lighting and 'Parkplaetze und Parkgaragen in Meran'; share capital 20 million euro, 100% held by the municipality. The page gives no locations, capacities or tariffs for car parks.

corrected_summary: Merano (Meran) charges for on-street parking through Blue Park zones: under the ordinance, Zone A is paid every day and Zone B Monday to Saturday (08:00-19:00), with a Zone C reserved for tourist coaches; the city's general parking page simplifies this to Monday to Sunday. The municipal executive decided in December 2022 to adjust the hourly rates (2.50 euro in Zone A, 1.50 euro in Zone B) from the start of 2023, and residents without a private space can apply for subscriptions; the sources do not show whether those rates are still current in 2026. The historic centre is a camera-enforced restricted traffic zone with four monitored entry points. The city council approved the mobility plan (PUMS) and traffic plan (PGTU) on 11 March 2025. The big structural change is the 594-space Kavernengarage under the Küchelberg, a public-private project financed by private partners (the investor group Meran Centrum Parking AG) in return for a 50-year concession; in February 2025 it was reported to be due to open together with the Küchelberg tunnel in autumn 2026, but the city's 7 October 2026 release gives no separate garage opening date or price. That release plans the bypass opening ceremony for 21 November and traffic release for 26 November 2026, and first city-centre measures from January 2027, including a reorganisation of central-area parking linked to the new garage; a hospital shuttle is only an idea. The province's planned station mobility centre (about 350 underground commuter spaces in a December 2024 report) now has construction expected in 2028-2029 according to the city. The hospital car park is reported full on school-term weekday mornings, and three Landtag members report heavy use of the Therme Meran garage (347,598 vehicles in a year) and expect lower revenue if traffic really leaves the centre. Live availability of city-centre car parks is said to be on mobility.meran.eu, but that site could not be read.
